operations.evidence: The provisional CSEW response rate for the year ending March 2026 was 48%; the ONS quality review found little impact on the reliability of crime estimates.
The lower response rate remains a quality consideration and does not remove sampling uncertainty.
Police recorded crime figures are supplied through the Home Office by the 43 territorial forces and British Transport Police.
Differences in recording practice and police activity can affect comparability between forces and periods.
Police recorded crime coverage follows the Notifiable Offence List and excludes non-notifiable matters such as anti-social behaviour and parking offences.
Excluded incidents must not be silently added to or inferred from notifiable crime totals.
Neither the CSEW nor police recorded crime provides a complete count of crime; both have exclusions and supplementary sources are used for a fuller picture.
A combined national picture still does not create exact incident or parcel attribution.
The CSEW is the most reliable indicator for long-term trends in common crime because it includes unreported crime and is unaffected by police activity or reporting-rate changes.
The survey remains subject to sampling error and non-sampling error such as recall problems.
Police recorded crime can show demand and policing effort, but for many crime types it is not a reliable measure of levels or trends and is not designated as accredited official statistics.
Recorded volumes can change because of reporting willingness, police activity and recording practice rather than underlying incidence alone.
The 23 July 2026 TACT release covers Great Britain up to 31 March 2026 and combines accredited official statistics, official statistics and statistics in development.
Administrative case data are updated as cases progress, so figures can be revised.
There were 3,061 terrorism-related arrests in the year ending March 2026; 2,819 were linked to supporting Palestine Action after its proscription on 5 July 2025.
The exceptional event-specific component dominates the annual change and should not be used as a general local terrorism trend.
Excluding arrests linked to supporting Palestine Action, there were 242 terrorism-related arrests, 44 of them in January to March 2026.
National arrest counts do not identify exposure or risk at a specific property.
At the data-provision date, 551 of 3,061 arrests, or 18%, had resulted in a charge.
Many cases were unfinished, so charge counts and rates can increase in later releases.
There were 41 arrested individuals aged 17 or under; minors represented 17% of non-Palestine Action arrests where age was known.
Small national demographic counts must not be converted into local risk profiles.
Seventy-two people were tried for terrorism-related offences in the year ending March 2026, and 273 people were in custody for terrorism or terrorism-connected offences at 31 March 2026.
Court and prison totals describe criminal-justice activity, not parcel-level public safety.
The Metropolitan Police Service conducted 98 section 43 stops and searches and other England and Wales forces conducted 108; the latter series is published as Official Statistics in Development.
Stop-and-search counts are operational measures and the developing series requires cautious comparison.
When a person is charged with multiple offences at the same time, the TACT statistics count only the most serious offence under the principal offence rule.
The resulting figures count people charged rather than every charge and must not be interpreted as total offence counts.
All 30 wave52 source IDs are unique and use a new indexed prefix.
Zero source roles were promoted to exact-address evidence, parcel risk, candidate values or business rows.
30 source rows and 64 operation rows were prepared for line-by-line website visibility.
No second runner, queue replacement, runtime execution, database write or business-data write was performed.
